subject: Urgent: Quantico production timeouts & retry amplification — proposed remediation and next steps
messages:
From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@quantico-apps.com>
To: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Luz Martinez <luz.martinez@quantico-apps.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T02:35:00Z
Subject: High 5xx/429 rates causing client timeouts — immediate help required

Monica —

We started seeing a sharp spike in 5xx and 429 responses across our inference routes around 02:12 UTC this morning. Error rate peaked at ~32% for the short window (10:12–10:34 PDT) and many of our client SDKs entered aggressive retry loops which compounded the overload.

Impact: several user-facing features timed out (authored content rendering & real-time suggestions). Throughput dropped ≈40% for our production cluster and latency p90 jumped from 120ms to ~2.4s. Our observability team collected logs and a short timeline; attaching the logs and a quick spreadsheet.

We need:
- Immediate mitigation to stop the retry amplification (throttles, circuit-breaker changes, or temporary fallback model).
- An incident timeline and an initial root-cause hypothesis.
- A clear remediation and credit discussion — this outage hit our revenue-critical paths during a peak window.

I’m escalating to our CTO and product leads shortly if we don’t get a firm plan in the next 2 hours. Please treat as P0.

Attachments: error-logs-20260910.txt, service-incident-timeline.xlsx

—Sam
Sam Turner
Head of Platform Engineering, Quantico Apps

From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@quantico-apps.com>
Cc: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Luz Martinez <luz.martinez@quantico-apps.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T02:50:00Z
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 rates causing client timeouts — immediate help required

Sam — thank you for the heads-up and the artifacts. I’m really sorry Quantico hit this.

Quick plan:
1) I’ve asked our infra SRE (Rachel) to take lead on triage and to push a hotfix today.
2) Please pause aggressive client-side retries (even a short backoff) if you can — that will buy immediate headroom.
3) We’ll propose a short mitigation (throttle + fallback to smaller model instance) that we can flip in <20 minutes.

I’m cc’ing Hannah (AM) to coordinate SLAs / credits and to loop in legal if needed. We’ll push an incident update in ~60 minutes with concrete mitigations applied and an ETA for a full RCA.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@quantico-apps.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Luz Martinez <luz.martinez@quantico-apps.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T03:05:00Z
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 rates causing client timeouts — immediate help required

Sam / Monica — rapid triage notes below (initial, will expand to full RCA):

What we see:
- Autoscales were slow to provision additional instances for one of the model pools due to a transient cloud API throttling event; backlog built up.
- A misconfigured circuit-breaker policy allowed retries to be reissued too quickly which amplified request load on the warmup path.
- Error signatures are 5xx on the serving infra + 429 from the gateway when token-bucket limits were hit.

Actions taken (completed within first 25 minutes):
- Applied temporary rate-limiter at the gateway to reduce retry amplification.
- Rolled a small model-fallback route (lower-cost quantized variant) for hot endpoints — cut latency p90 by ~30% in the test shard.
- Adjusted circuit-breaker thresholds to increase backoff windows.

Next steps (today):
- Full RCA with timeline and patch (ETA: 2026-09-12T15:00:00Z).
- Postmortem and durable config change to autoscaler jitter and circuit-breaker defaults (ETA: one week).

Preliminary credit framing: we will propose an incident remediation package (usage credit + operational commitments). Hannah will coordinate the commercial offer.

Attachments included: service-incident-timeline.xlsx, proposed-mitigations.patch

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@quantico-apps.com>
To: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Luz Martinez <luz.martinez@quantico-apps.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T04:12:00Z
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 rates causing client timeouts — immediate help required

Thanks for the quick mitigation steps — we saw improved behavior after you rolled the fallback variant and applied the rate-limiter. A few follow-ups from our side:

- We need a concrete SLA-credit calculation and justification for the outage window. Please include how you will compute credit against our committed reserved capacity vs. host usage.
- We expect a signed RCA and an operational plan we can present to our execs by Tuesday’s EOD (2026-09-15).
- Quantico will need an assurance that autoscaler jitter + CB config changes will be enforced globally; otherwise we’ll ask for contractual remediation.

We are pausing expansion trials pending the RCA and credit offer.

—Sam

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@quantico-apps.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Luz Martinez <luz.martinez@quantico-apps.com>
Date: 2026-09-11T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 rates causing client timeouts — immediate help required

Sam — I’m very sorry for the disruption. On behalf of Redwood, we want to make this right. Proposed commercial remediation (initial offer):

1) One-time incident credit equal to $12,500 applied to your next invoice (represents ~25% of estimated impacted usage for the incident window).
2) 90 days of Redwood Optimize (premium insights & batching recommendations) at no charge to help prevent recurrence and optimize unit cost.

If Quantico prefers an SLA-based percentage credit instead, we can provide a formal calculation (percent of monthly committed spend prorated for the impacted window) — legal and finance will prepare a formal statement.

Operational commitments we’ll include in the RCA:
- Full timeline + root cause with code/infra references.
- Deployable autoscaler jitter and circuit-breaker defaults enforced across regions.
- Two follow-up check-ins at 30/90 days to review telemetry and prevent regressions.

If this offer is acceptable, I’ll have the finance team draft an invoice credit memo and a short amendment for the operational commitments. We can do an exec call tomorrow (2026-09-12 at 16:00 PDT) to finalize.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@quantico-apps.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Luz Martinez <luz.martinez@quantico-apps.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T17:10:00Z
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 rates causing client timeouts — immediate help required

Sam / Luz — thank you for pushing this through. Quick summary and next actions to align execs:

- Status: temporary mitigations remain in place (gateway rate-limiter + fallback route). Production metrics show error rates back to baseline and latency recovering.
- RCA ETA: 2026-09-15T23:59:00Z (we’re targeting the EOD window you requested).
- Commercial: Hannah proposed a one-time credit ($12,500) + 90 days of Redwood Optimize. If Quantico prefers a different credit structure (e.g., percent-based under SLA), please let Hannah know and we’ll get finance/legal to finalize.
- Exec call: proposed 2026-09-12T23:00Z UTC / 16:00 PDT tomorrow — invite will follow.

We take this seriously and will own the operational fixes. I’ll keep oversight until RCA is delivered. Please confirm whether the credit offer is acceptable or if you want the percent-based SLA calculation.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
Attachments: service-incident-timeline.xlsx (final), error-logs-20260910.txt (redacted)
